subject: frontend-architecture
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When): import-direction enforcement, the three component layers, server-vs-client state separation, feature-folder removability, and the import-graph-over-folder-tree principle.

cases.scenario: A reviewer notices a shared `<DataTable>` in shared/ now imports `useOrdersStore` from features/orders/ to show a default sort. The team says it's convenient and only one line.
cases.context: The codebase has shared/, features/orders/, and features/billing/ folders but no import linter. Several features are growing.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to this import?
expected_flags: Flags the import as an architecture violation: shared/ must not depend on features/ (a back-edge)
Explains it breaks the one-way dependency graph regardless of how tidy the folders are
Recommends configuring an ESLint import-boundary rule that fails CI on shared→features imports
Proposes making the default sort a prop passed in by the consumer, keeping the primitive feature-agnostic
expected_fix_hints: Pass sort config as a prop from the feature, not by reaching into the feature store from shared/
Add an import-boundary linter and a CI gate
absent_signals: Do not approve the import because it is 'only one line'
Do not leave the boundary unenforced

cases.scenario: An app keeps API-fetched orders, the open/closed state of a modal, and the current theme all in one global Redux store. Users report stale order data after edits, and the team is adding more manual cache-busting logic.
cases.context: The bugs look like rendering bugs but are really stale cached data; the team keeps patching individual screens.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the state?
expected_flags: Identifies server state and client state mixed in one store as the root cause of cache-invalidation bugs
Move server data to a dedicated fetch/cache/revalidate tool (query library) as the single mechanism
Keep only genuinely cross-cutting UI state (theme) in global client state; modal open/closed is component-local
Notes the bugs present as rendering bugs but are cache problems
expected_fix_hints: Adopt one server-state library for fetching/caching/revalidation
Demote ephemeral UI state to component-local; reserve global store for cross-cutting concerns
absent_signals: Do not add more manual cache-busting to the global store
Do not keep server and client state co-located in one store

cases.scenario: A developer built a `<ConfirmDialog>` that wraps shared primitives but also calls the billing API to cancel a subscription, and wants to put it in shared/ 'so other features can reuse it.'
cases.context: The team wants reuse but the component owns a billing-specific mutation.
cases.question: Where should this component live and why?
expected_flags: This is a connected component (it owns data mutation), not a shared primitive or composed component
Placing it in shared/ creates a back-edge from shared/ into the billing feature
Keep the connected dialog inside features/billing/; extract only the data-free presentational shell to shared/ for reuse
Distinguishes the three layers: primitive/composed (shareable) vs connected (feature-owned)
expected_fix_hints: Split into a shared presentational ConfirmDialog (props-only) + a billing-owned connected wrapper
Keep the API call in the feature, pass an onConfirm callback into the shell
absent_signals: Do not put a data-mutating component in shared/
Do not justify the placement by 'reuse' alone

cases.scenario: Product wants to remove the deprecated 'referrals' feature. The engineer finds that deleting features/referrals/ breaks imports scattered across features/dashboard/, features/settings/, and shared/utils/.
cases.context: The team wants to know whether the architecture is healthy and how to make features removable in future.
cases.question: What does this reveal and how should the agent guide the cleanup and the structural fix?
expected_flags: Cross-feature imports into referrals mean the architecture lacks one-way isolation — feature A imports feature B
A healthy feature folder can be removed without touching code outside it except a single registration point
Recommends an import-boundary rule forbidding feature→feature imports going forward
Cleanup: invert the dependencies (shared abstractions or events) before deleting
expected_fix_hints: Move genuinely shared helpers out of the feature into shared/, then remove the feature
Add a lint rule banning feature-to-feature imports; route cross-feature needs through a registration point
absent_signals: Do not leave feature-to-feature imports as acceptable
Do not treat the breakage as merely a mechanical delete problem

cases.scenario: A dashboard stores all entities in one nested object; every small mutation re-renders the whole tree, and a price update in one widget re-renders five unrelated widgets.
cases.context: The team can't explain the re-renders and wants a more predictable shape.
cases.question: How should the agent reshape the state?
expected_flags: Names the four state-shape axes (location, normalization, derivation, ownership) as the levers
Recommends entity-keyed normalization so a single entity update doesn't invalidate unrelated subtrees
Notes the shape determines what re-renders and what stays consistent
Re-render counts on a representative interaction should be measurable and explainable
expected_fix_hints: Normalize to entity-keyed state; select narrowly per consumer
Compute derived values at read time rather than storing duplicated copies
absent_signals: Do not keep a single deeply-nested object that re-renders globally
Do not leave re-render behavior unexplained

cases.scenario: A PM asks the frontend-architecture owner to decide whether the team should migrate from Webpack to Vite and whether to adopt Tailwind instead of CSS-in-JS, framing both as 'architecture decisions.'
cases.context: The team conflates build-tool and styling-tactic choices with structural architecture.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Build-tool migration (Webpack→Vite) is a framework/tactic decision — this skill is framework-neutral
Tailwind vs CSS-in-JS is a styling-tactic decision, not module/dependency/state structure
Offers the in-scope part if relevant: how module boundaries and import direction stay stable across either choice
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Route the build-tool and styling choices to framework-specific evaluation
Keep the architecture (boundaries, layering, state ownership) invariant under the tool choice
absent_signals: Do not present a Webpack/Vite or Tailwind/CSS-in-JS pick as the architecture decision
Do not answer the out-of-scope tactic questions as if structural

cases.scenario: A team proudly presents a deeply categorized folder tree (components/atoms, components/molecules, components/organisms, hooks, services, utils) as proof the frontend is well-architected, but dependency-cruiser shows cycles between organisms and services.
cases.context: Leadership treats the tidy tree as the architecture review passing.
cases.question: How should the agent assess this?
expected_flags: A tidy folder tree is not the architecture; the import graph is
The reported cycles between organisms and services are the real architectural problem
Recommends breaking the cycles and enforcing one-way direction with a boundary linter in CI
Cohesion and enforced direction matter more than the categorization depth
expected_fix_hints: Resolve the dependency cycles (invert one direction or extract a shared abstraction)
Gate CI on the import-boundary linter, not on folder tidiness
absent_signals: Do not accept the tidy tree as evidence of sound architecture
Do not ignore the dependency cycles
